brief: Deutsche Bank's monthly dislocations note argues the current market equilibrium is unsustainable. Since last month's goldilocks piece, a bond selloff has pushed yields to multi-year highs, but rates markets still price only limited tightening while inflation pressure builds. Brent is $96/bbl against $82.49/bbl a month ago on renewed US-Iran strikes, European gas futures are at their highest since early 2023, and August food prices jumped, with sugar +21.5%, wheat +18.3% and corn +16.8%. So either inflation falls or pressure on rates continues, and sustained rate pressure forces an adjustment in risk assets. Four dislocations follow. Fed pricing implies a shallow hiking cycle even though ISM services prices paid hit a 4-year high consistent with 5% CPI, and futures price a 60% hike probability. ECB pricing for June 2027 has gone from 74bps of hikes to 72bps despite higher inflation swaps and upside growth surprises. The oil curve stays downward-sloping, with 6-month Brent at $83.2/bbl, assuming a Hormuz reopening that keeps not happening. Equities and credit stay complacent as the US 10-year real yield is up over 70bps, and rate cuts and fiscal stimulus are less available as cushions.
